page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside 62.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction support spans AVX-512 extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, as well as cryptographic accelerations such as AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance. Single-core tests in stress-ng reach the top 10% tier with a score of 3449.99, mirrored by compression tests where single-threaded gzip reaches 37.95 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaches 16.86 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals strong throughput, logging a PassMark memory score of 2787.78 in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, large-block memory read and write bandwidths, and web serving throughput align within the middle 50% tier across comparable configurations.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely on external network-attached block storage for persistence. In terms of cost efficiency, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a standard footprint for sustained enterprise workloads, trading off raw multi-threaded throughput density for elevated per-core compute responsiveness.

Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16 is suited for multi-tier web applications, medium-scale relational databases, caching systems such as Redis, and CI/CD build environments that benefit from elevated single-thread instruction throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-16 is a general-purpose compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor. The configuration delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 62.0 GB of memory, resulting in roughly 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It incorporates modern instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-decile single-core compute and data decompression throughput alongside strong memory test scores, while multi-core workloads and memory bandwidth operate at average baseline levels. The instance does not include local disk storage or physical GPUs, utilizing network storage for disk operations. Because of its balanced resource ratio and pronounced per-core execution speed, the c4d-standard-16 is tailored for workloads including static and dynamic web serving, relational databases, caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines.
